title: Engine subcommand JSON contracts
summary: Seventeen Runtime-called subcommands over request-file JSON and stdout JSON. Artifacts remain under the authorized sandbox roots. The engine never owns account identity, Project governance, budgets or durable result publication.

carrier.notes: Original: lumeri-engine <subcommand> <request.json> [<output-root>], running lumeri-engine, for its other subcommands in its sandbox profile. Replacement: a lumeri.engine.program/v1 capability with module "lumeri.engine.gemia", naming an executable file of its Luc, started with the original's arguments, environment and profile, writing only the session scratch (luc_engine_programs, sandbox.MacOSSandboxExecutor.bind_capability).

replaceability.why: A replacement is code. It is one executable file of a Luc that holds engine.program, which Lumeri's review of its exact bytes grants, and it stands in for lumeri-engine, for its other subcommands: the Runtime starts it with the same arguments, environment, working directory and sandbox profile, except that it may write only the session scratch, never the Project. It runs only on a machine with a sandbox (macOS today) (docs/luc/engine-programs.md).
replaceability.decided: today's code: lumeri_engine_cli.py:99-137; Acrab 2026-10-26: replaced by engine programs in the engine's own sandbox

reach.notes: The program reads what the original may read and writes only the session scratch; it runs only what the original may run (the profile's executables), with no network. The Runtime checks what it leaves and keeps the Project, the cache and the events.

operations.name: quanta
operations.notes: No fixed operation deadline is enforced; the enclosing authorized sandbox profile supplies its execution ceiling. Input is the JSON object read from request.json; output is stdout JSON on a successful CLI exit. Exit statuses are engine.cli. No standalone CLI idempotency: retries rerun computation or rewrite scratch. Durable Project import/commit is separate and cannot be treated as one atomic write. One PNG per declared visible state; exact frame count and output-root confinement checked. Runtime bounds frame count to 2048; failures are nonzero process exits.

events.name: luc.module_fell_back
events.notes: Once per Session in a start: when the module's program broke (gate run), or when its Luc was left off for the module after three breaks (gate load). Codes: E_LUC_ENGINE_START, E_LUC_ENGINE_EXIT, E_LUC_ENGINE_RESULT, E_LUC_ENGINE_LIMIT, E_LUC_ENGINE_DEADLINE, E_LUC_ENGINE_CHANGED.

invariants.text: A subcommand computes or writes scratch artifacts only; Runtime retains final Project commit and revision authority.
When the program breaks after writing in the session scratch, the scratch is restored to its state before the program ran, so the original sees none of what the program wrote.

break: the program cannot be placed, or its bytes are not the ones its Luc loaded with
it does not start in the sandbox, exits with a status other than 0, or leaves a process behind
it outruns the profile's time, memory, process or output limits

its stdout or declared files are not what the original's would be: Its stdout is one JSON value and the files it declares exist; the Runtime's checks after the run hold them as they hold the engine's.
failure.notes: The original runs the same request at once, and every request of this module for the rest of the start (luc_interactions.note_module_break); three breaks of the same bytes leave the Luc off for the module at later starts until reset (luc_breaker, luc_cli.py modules reset lumeri.engine.gemia). The creator stopping the request is not a break: the program is stopped and nothing runs in its place.

conformance.notes: tests/test_luc_engine_programs.py holds the load gate, which runs belong to which module, and, with real compiled programs in the media sandbox, an answer in place of FFprobe and FFmpeg, every way of breaking handing the same request to the original, the scratch-only fence, a stop that is not a break, and a real Worker whose measured facts are the program's until it breaks. The engine's own modules share that path; no engine subcommand is replaced by a real program in a test yet.

known_deviations.text: Several subcommands serialize arbitrary caught exception class names as error_code. The listed codes are known literals on those paths, not a claim that the set is closed; affected operations remain draft until stable error envelopes are defined.
Beyond one JSON value on stdout and the declared files, a program's answer meets the Runtime's own checks only after the run; a failure there is the request's, and the original does not run it again.
